set.st: A deathbed story said a settler buried gold here around the Civil War. In 1943 the legislature actually passed a law (House File 934, Chapter 357) letting a treasure seeker dig on state grounds. On 10 June 1943 the treasure hunters dug a few yards from the Soldiers' Home administration building, guided by a witching rod, with state officials watching and a legislator standing on the bond; the paper's verdict next day: 'there was no treasure.' LiDAR cache check (USGS 1 m, 2022): Nothing that fits the story stands out within the search area: the pits and lines it finds there are ditches, banks, ponds or natural ground.
set.t: State veterans' home grounds: no detecting without permission. Mostly a fun piece of law history. The 1943 bill names only state land along the river near the city limits, but the June 1943 dig report puts the hunt at the Soldiers' Home administration building, so the link is period.

src: Minneapolis Star, 11 Jun 1943, p. 17 (the dig: no treasure)
